subject.title: Anthropic setup-token onboarding path has multiple failure modes (docs gap, credential propagation, multi-agent sync)

question: Should Anthropic setup-token/static token auth be physically synced to sibling agent SQLite stores, inherited through runtime/read-through only, or exposed through an explicit operator-controlled repair/sync action?
rationale: Each viable fix changes how sensitive provider credentials move across agent stores, and prior same-repo PRs were closed after auth-file and OAuth fanout concerns, so automation should not choose the permanent credential boundary.

options.title: Operator-controlled token repair or sync
options.body: Add doctor/status or models-auth repair behavior that validates the main token profile and copies only portable static token credentials after explicit user confirmation.

options.title: Runtime inheritance plus validation
options.body: Keep credentials in the main store and improve startup/runtime validation and docs so secondary agents resolve inherited profiles without physical copies.

options.title: Automatic static-token sibling sync
options.body: Copy portable Anthropic token profiles to sibling stores during setup-token and paste-token onboarding while explicitly excluding OAuth refresh credentials.

recommendation.title: Operator-controlled token repair or sync
recommendation.body: Add doctor/status or models-auth repair behavior that validates the main token profile and copies only portable static token credentials after explicit user confirmation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across provider auth helpers, Anthropic auth direction, and auth-store inheritance semantics.
